chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thal'aba, from Zurara, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the prayer behind the adversaries, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are not in my presence except at the status of the walls.'

key_terms.الْمُخَالِفِينَ: The adversaries / those who differ (referring to non-Shia)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying behind non-Shia Muslims according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Zurara ibn A'yan asks Imam al-Baqir (AS) about praying behind non-Shia Muslims, to which the Imam replies, 'They are to me only like walls.' This metaphor signifies that while their prayer is valid and their presence in the row is permissible, they are spiritually distinct and separate from the Shia, lacking the unity of faith and leadership (Imamate) that defines the Shia congregation. This view supports the permissibility of praying in congregations with other Muslims while maintaining a distinct Shia identity and spiritual boundary.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba, from Zurara who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Salāt behind the adversaries. So heasws said: ‘They are not in myasws presence except at the status of the walls (bunch of bricks)’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by Ahmad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal from Tha’labah from Zurarah who has said the following:
“I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about performing Salah (prayer) behind those who oppose our belief. He (the Imam) said, ‘To me they are but walls (scarecrows).”’
